db_host.description: Hostname or IP address of the PostgreSQL server to connect to.

db_port.description: Port number of the PostgreSQL server.

db_user.description: Database user account for pg_fact_loader to authenticate as.

db_password.description: Password for the database user. Prefer using .pgpass or IAM auth in production.

db_name.description: Name of the PostgreSQL database to connect to.

log_level.description: Minimum severity level for log messages to emit.

log_file.description: Path to the log file (standard output if empty).

worker_count.description: Number of concurrent worker processes to spawn.

max_tasks_per_worker.description: Maximum number of tasks a worker may process before restarting (helps avoid memory leaks).

task_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds a single fact table build may run before being killed.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between checks for new fact table build requests in the job queue.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retry attempts after a failed task.

max_retry_delay_seconds.description: Maximum delay (seconds) between retries (capped exponential backoff).

fact_tables.description: List of fact tables to manage. Each entry defines the source query and refresh behavior.

name.description: Human-readable identifier for the fact table (used in logs/metrics).

schema.description: PostgreSQL schema where the fact table resides.

table.description: Name of the fact table to build or refresh.

query.description: SQL statement used to generate the fact table data. Typically an INSERT/SELECT or CTAS query.

schedule.description: Cron expression for automatic background refresh (e.g., '0 2 * * *' = daily at 2 AM). Leave blank to disable scheduled runs.

truncate_before_load.description: If true, TRUNCATE the table before loading new data (full refresh). If false, perform append/update.

tags.description: Optional labels to categorize or group this fact table (e.g., 'finance', 'realtime').

monitoring.enabled.description: Enable the built-in HTTP health/metrics endpoint.

monitoring.port.description: Port to expose the monitoring endpoint on.

monitoring.path.description: HTTP path for health checks (e.g., /health or /metrics).
